papers.title: Thirty years of 2D MIT
papers.abstract: The zero-magnetic-field metal-insulator transition in strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems was experimentally discovered three decades ago, thereby triggering extensive experimental and theoretical investigations. Prior to this discovery, the occurrence of such a transition --- as well as the very existence of a metallic phase in two dimensions --- was regarded as forbidden within the framework of the one-parameter scaling theory of localization. In this work, we provide a comprehensive review of the transport and thermodynamic properties of two-dimensional electron and hole systems in which carrier-carrier interactions constitute the dominant energy scale. We present and critically analyze both experimental observations and theoretical developments accumulated over the past thirty years.

papers.title: Disentangling Multiple Scaling Dimensions via Operator Covariance in Critical Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We present a general proof of different power-law decays versus distance of the eigenvalues of two-point covariance matrices in critical lattice quantum models, allowing extraction of multiple scaling dimensions. We demonstrate the practical utility of this method in the context of a spin-1/2 chain with critical ground state described by the SU(2)_1 Wess--Zumino--Witten field theory. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute covariance matrices in different symmetry sectors, we resolve the expected relevant and marginal primary operators as well as some descendants. The covariance method can be integrated into many existing numerical schemes and promises to significantly enhance computational studies of quantum criticality.

papers.title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
papers.abstract: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $μ_q$ and $μ_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordström black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $ω,k,T,μ_3\llμ_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $ω,k,μ_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.

papers.title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
papers.abstract: Conformal defects describe impurities and boundaries at criticality. Their stability depends on the scaling dimensions of operators localized on the defects, but these dimensions are often difficult to determine. We derive analytic upper bounds on the lowest nonvacuum scaling dimension using only two defect entropies and the dimension of a defect-changing operator. The bounds identify when relevant operators must appear on the defect with larger defect entropy. They follow from the conformal bootstrap of four-point functions of defect-changing operators and apply to unitary conformal line defects and to conformal boundaries in two-dimensional CFTs. The Ising and Potts models provide exact checks. In three-dimensional $O(N)$ models, we apply the bounds to direct sums of pinning field defects with symmetry-related orientations. Data from a single such defect exclude stable impurity order with three or more orientations in $O(2)$ and $O(3)$, or four or more in $O(4)$, for any geometry of the orientations, and require a relevant domain-wall operator between individually stable pinning field defects at every nonzero relative angle up to $120^\circ$ in $O(3)$ and up to $109.47^\circ$ in $O(4)$. A direct fuzzy-sphere computation of the lowest domain-wall dimension at different relative angles for $N=2,3,4$ is consistent with these bounds and indicates that, within this class of impurities, only two-state order remains a candidate for stable order in $O(3)$ and $O(4)$, while none survives in $O(2)$. A separate application to AdS/BCFT shows that, at fixed unequal brane tensions, a light boundary-condition-changing operator requires additional light primaries on the boundary with larger boundary entropy.

papers.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

papers.title: Defect Anomalies at a Distance
papers.abstract: Surface defects carry Weyl and gravitational anomalies that generalize the central charges of two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) and characterize the anomalous response of gapless surface modes to background geometry. These anomalies usually appear as contact terms on the defect. We explain how they are encoded at a distance, in scheme-independent integrated bulk stress-tensor correlators. We derive sum rules for them in terms of defect operator data, establish a lower bound on the boundary Weyl anomaly in three-dimensional CFTs, and illustrate our results with explicit examples.

papers.title: Direct transition from a fractional Chern insulator to a topological superconductor
papers.abstract: We find numerical evidence for a direct continuous transition from a Laughlin fractional Chern insulator (FCI) to a $c_-=3/2$ topological superconductor (TSC), driven by increasing bandwidth at filling $ν=1/3$ in a repulsively interacting Chern band. At the critical point, the electron correlation length diverges at momentum away from the reference Fermi surface. We develop a generalized theory of superconducting-vortex proliferation for this transition. Magnetic translation organizes the vortices into six valleys, so translation-preserving proliferation requires additional gauge fields. The resulting theory reproduces the momentum structure of the critical spectrum and captures the divergent electron correlation. Upon doping away from commensurate filling, the theory gives rise to a superconducting dome. These results are consistent with an anyonic origin of the topological superconductivity in the absence of a weak-coupling Fermi-surface instability.

papers.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
papers.abstract: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.

papers.title: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
papers.abstract: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap. We show that a ``blind'' preparation, designed from the clean chain without knowledge of the disorder realisation or its distribution, can start farther from stationarity yet overtake a reference in typical samples of a dephased disordered XX chain. It requires only the chain geometry and the particle number. At strong dephasing, the density dynamics maps to a resistor chain, and an exact inverse-generator identity links the residual overlap to the spatial resistance profile. We find two distinct thresholds: a finite mean resistance suffices for diffusion, but the residual overlap decays as $L^{-1/2}$ with chain length $L$ only when the resistance variance is finite; rare weak links slow this decay. We predict the fraction of samples in which the blind preparation wins, which is an ensemble-level measure of its reliability. Finite-size calculations support both scaling regimes with interactions at strong dephasing. We give preparation circuits and a density readout for the residual overlap.

papers.title: Anisotropy lifts topological protection of transport in pumped spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate the prospect of topological spin pumping and transport in a dimerized spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ anisotropic XY chain with tunable in-plane anisotropy. Through a Jordan-Wigner transformation, the system maps onto an extended Rice-Mele-type fermionic model whose momentum-space band structure exhibits gapped regions characterized by nonzero Chern numbers ($\pm 1$) as well as trivial and gapless regimes. Conventional momentum-space analysis therefore predicts quantized Thouless-type spin pumping in parts of the Chern number diagram. However, real-space time evolution under open boundary conditions reveals that the spin transport is generally not quantized away from the isotropic limit. In the anisotropic regime, eigen-energy states within the transporting subspace hybridize during the driving cycle, leading to a transport that depends on details of the driving protocol. Quantized pumping and transport survive only in the isotropic limit, where the Hamiltonian reduces to decoupled Rice-Mele sectors and the transported spin component is conserved. Our results demonstrate that momentum-space topological invariants alone do not guarantee quantized spin transport in anisotropic spin chains. More broadly, they show that the conventional Thouless-pumping framework does not straightforwardly extend to situations where the transported quantity is not conserved, highlighting the importance of real-space diagnostics in topological transport phenomena.

papers.title: Multimagnon bound states in the polarized phase of anisotropic antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: We investigate single-ion bound magnon states in the high-field polarized phase of uniaxial antiferromagnets. By solving the two-particle problem exactly, we determine the dispersion of bound magnon pairs both below and above the continuum. We also obtain rigorous bounds on their binding energies by using the Gershgorin circle theorem. For spin-1 easy-axis systems, two-magnon bound states with zero total momentum emerge as low-energy excitations once the ratio of single-ion anisotropy to exchange exceeds a threshold value. As the field decreases, magnon pairs condense, driving a transition into a spin-nematic phase. Beyond the two-magnon problem, we develop a general strong-coupling approach that describes $n$-magnon single-ion bound states ($n\leq 2S$) in large-$S$ easy-axis antiferromagnets. The Bose-Einstein condensation of these multi-magnon excitations yields a rich hierarchy of field-induced multipolar phases stabilized by single-ion anisotropy. Comparisons with recent experiments on Na$_2$BaNi(PO$_4$)$_2$ and Sr$_2$CoGe$_2$O$_7$ illustrate the quantitative power of our theory.

papers.title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries. We demonstrate that matrix product operators enable the explicit construction of intertwiners between the dual theories and their (non-invertible) symmetries. With closed boundary conditions, we can relate the full spectrum of these dual theories by considering all possible twisted boundary conditions. We illustrate how the Peter-Weyl transform appears when the duality acts on the boundary Hilbert space of a $G$-symmetric model. The presented framework generalizes previous work on dualities for unitary fusion category symmetric models. It exemplifies how dualities for both finite and continuous symmetries rely on the relation between a bond algebra and a representation of the symmetry in the lattice as double centralizers. We argue that dual non-invertible spontaneous symmetry breaking is the mechanism that underlies symmetric tensor network algorithms. We illustrate these results for $U(1)$- and $SU(2)$-symmetric quantum lattice models.

papers.title: Spin supersolid in triangular lattice easy-axis spin-1/2 antiferromagnet: a fermionic parton perspective
papers.abstract: We study the supersolid order of the spin-1/2 easy-axis XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice using a fermionic parton mean-field theory built on the $π$-flux Dirac spin liquid, with the mean-field order generated by an on-site spinon interaction term and nearest-neighbor (anisotropic) spin couplings. The collective modes are obtained using the random-phase approximation (RPA). In a finite parameter region, we find the Y state as a self-consistent solution, together with the competing Y' state, which is a $90^\circ$-rotated Y state inside the order plane. The mean-field energy favors Y', even though the two states are exactly degenerate in the classical limit. However, the Y state can become lower in energy when higher-order corrections due to the fluctuations of the collective modes are considered. The Y state can also be stabilized on the mean-field level by applying small external fields, which we do in two different ways: moment-aligned local field and uniform field along the easy axis. In both cases, the RPA calculation for the stabilized Y state gives a roton minimum at the $M$ point in the excitation spectrum. A gapped pseudo-Goldstone mode above the gapless Goldstone mode is obtained as well, which has also been observed experimentally. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of tuning the spinon interaction strength and the anisotropy in spin couplings in our phenomenological model. Comparison with the recent numerical and experimental results is also discussed.

papers.title: Accessing Fractional Wilson Lines from U(1) Monodromy Defects on the Fuzzy Sphere
papers.abstract: Wilson lines are gauge-invariant probes of charge screening and deconfinement, which can detect the response of quantum critical matter to an external charge, but their universal information at strongly-coupled critical points remains hard to access. Here we investigate a continuous family of $U(1)$ monodromy defects of the three-dimensional $O(2)$ Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory, which is dual to fractional Wilson lines in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model with one unit-charged scalar. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe the emergence of charged operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy. The appearance of displacement operator at its protected dimension supports the conformal nature of this defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving defect scalar, and identify charge-one monopole operators as relevant symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the duality, these results provide non-perturbative evidence that fractional Wilson lines of the critical Abelian Higgs model are stable conformal lines.

papers.title: Key role of orbital exchange in CoO magnetism
papers.abstract: Co ions in the antiferromagnetic phase of CoO are known to possess a substantial orbital moment, making this material promising for orbitronic applications. However, intersite exchange interactions involving these orbital degrees of freedom remain poorly quantified, and their role in CoO magnetism is unclear. Here, we derive a full low-energy effective Hamiltonian for CoO, including orbital exchange terms, using an ab initio force-theorem approach based on DFT+dynamical mean-field theory. We find sizable orbital interactions, with quadrupolar orbital exchange emerging as the dominant nearest-neighbor term. The collinear antiferromagnetic order obtained from the effective Hamiltonian features magnetic moments tilted away from the pseudocubic <001> direction and an orbital contribution amounting to about one-third of the total moment, in agreement with experimental estimates. We show that the moment tilting originates from the combined effect of orbital and spin-orbital exchange interactions. The same interactions also produce a prominent splitting of the lowest excitation band. By directly modeling the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) intensity, we further show that the characteristic column-like structures previously observed in CoO INS provide a clear fingerprint of orbital exchange. We also discuss possible impact of our findings for further advances in the field of complex collective excitations, their transport properties and applications in the realm of orbitronics.

papers.title: Microscopic Origin and Josephson Signatures of $d$-Wave Superconductivity in Monolayer FeSe
papers.abstract: Monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$ exhibits high-temperature superconductivity with an electron-only Fermi surface, raising fundamental questions about its unconventional pairing mechanism. Motivated by recent Josephson scanning tunneling microscopy evidence for nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity, we investigate the microscopic role of the Fe $d_{xy}$ orbital using an experimentally constrained multiorbital theory. A tight-binding model fitted to quasiparticle interference and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals substantial $d_{xy}$ character near the Fermi level and dominant nearest-neighbor hopping, in contrast to the conventional kinetic-frustration picture of iron-based superconductors. Both itinerant spin-fluctuation calculations and strong-coupling exchange approaches favor a robust $d$-wave pairing state, whose interband pairing components allow a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum. We further establish a symmetry-based selection rule for spatial Josephson tunneling, revealing characteristic bond-centered maxima and mirror-enforced interference zeros that distinguish $d$-wave pairing from competing $s$-wave states. These symmetry-enforced nodal lines survive near Fe-site impurities, while a pronounced contrast between the $d$- and $s$-wave Josephson patterns persists around vortices despite the loss of mirror protection. Our results connect the unconventional $d_{xy}$ electronic structure to nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity and demonstrate the power of spatial Josephson interference for resolving pairing symmetry in multiorbital superconductors.

papers.title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
papers.abstract: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

papers.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model. Our results establish duality defects and generalized symmetries as practical resources for preparing and probing non-local excitations on quantum hardware.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count -- the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $G(iε)$ -- and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We demonstrate that the reported violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton diagram representation of physical quantities, thereby resolving a long-standing point of contention in many-body theory. Furthermore, we show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is itself a genuine topological invariant directly tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional $Φ[G]$ rather than to the Green's function alone. We demonstrate that this invariant, like the monodromy of $\ln G(iε)$ itself, stems exclusively from the zero-frequency discontinuity of the Matsubara trajectory.

papers.title: Contrasting fate of holes introduced by Fe or In in kagome metal CoSn
papers.abstract: CoSn is a kagome metal with well-defined flat bands 0.2 eV below the Fermi level EF. Moving them across EF would offer a rare opportunity to investigate their impact on electronic properties. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and X-ray absorption at the Co K-edge, we examine two routes to introduce holes in this compound, through Co/Fe or Sn/In substitutions. Substituting In for Sn produces an almost rigid upward shift of the bands toward EF, as expected for hole doping, whereas substituting Fe for Co leads to an unexpected downward shift. Density functional theory calculations reproduce these opposite trends and trace the unusual behavior of Fe to its local magnetic moment. The moment keeps the hole on the Fe impurity and imposes an attractive electrostatic potential on neighboring Co atoms. Overall, both substitutions bring weakly dispersing states close to EF, the flat bands of the Co kagome lattice upon In substitution and partly localized states around magnetic Fe impurities upon Fe substitution.

papers.title: Photoinduced switching of orbital-selective Mott states
papers.abstract: We investigate light-driven inversion of orbital selectivity in a two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model initially in an orbital-selective Mott phase. Using the matrix-product-state we show that tailored pulse excitations drive interorbital charge transfer that nearly reverses the orbital occupations. Single-particle spectral snapshots exhibit changes consistent with an interchange of the localized and itinerant characters of the orbitals. We analyze the relevant one- and two-photon excitation channels and show that chirping around the lower-frequency resonance enhances the transfer. These results establish a microscopic route to reversing orbital selectivity and accessing long-lived nonequilibrium states in multiorbital systems.

papers.title: Ground-state properties of uniaxial magnetic model for antiferromagnetic 1/1 periodic approximants to icosahedral quasicrystals
papers.abstract: The ground-state properties of the uniaxial magnetic model in the 1/1 periodic approximant to the icosahedral quasicrystal with antiferromagnetic interactions for the nearest-neighbor bond $J_1$ and the next-nearest-neighbor bond $J_2$ are analyzed theoretically. By performing numerically-exact calculation, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram for the interaction strength $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy defined within the mirror plane reflecting the effect of the crystalline electric field. We have discovered non-collinear magnetic structures, whose magnetic space groups are identified as the antiferromagnetic orders $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$ and $R_{\rm R}\bar{3}$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(111)$ as well as the antiferromagnetic orders $Im'm'm'$ and $R\bar{3}'$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(000)$ and the ferrimagnetic orders $Im'm'2$, $I2'2'2$, $P2'/m'$, and $P\bar{1}$. By analyzing each ground state with degeneracy, we have revealed the magnetic as well as topological properties, which are useful to analyze experimental observations of rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants considering the effect of magnetic domains.

papers.title: Fermi-volume anomaly in quartet condensates
papers.abstract: We investigate the relation between density and Fermi volume in a four-component Fermi system with quartet order. For a regular zero-temperature branch without pair order, we express the correction to the Fermi-volume count in terms of the response of the Luttinger-Ward functional to a phase winding of the quartet source. Its leading term is a weighted difference between four-particle and four-hole states. For a Gaussian vertex and parabolic dispersion, we find that the correction expands the Fermi volume in one dimension and contracts it in three dimensions in the parameter range studied. The sign in two dimensions depends on the momentum cutoff. We solve the one-dimensional Dyson equation at fixed density and compare the counting correction obtained from the Fermi points with that evaluated from the dressed spectra at low temperature. At fixed quartet amplitude and peak normalization of the vertex, the correction depends strongly on the vertex width, whereas the fermionic entropy changes little. We also examine the linear pairing response, which can limit the continuation of the unpaired branch to zero temperature.

papers.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

papers.title: Interfacial polarity control of anomalous Hall effect in LaCoO3-SrIrO3 heterostructures
papers.abstract: Interfacial polarity in oxide heterostructures can drive robust charge redistribution across the interface, yet its role in tailoring topological transport phenomena like the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) remains largely unexplored. Here, we control the sign of polarity-induced charge in SrIrO3-LaCoO3 interfaces by independently engineering the layer stacking sequence and the atomic termination. In-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy directly confirms the sign reversal of the induced charge in SrIrO3 through the contrasting electronic band shifts between different interfacial configurations. Magneto-transport measurements across a systematic matrix of four distinct heterostructures reveal that the AHE can be cleanly toggled on and off: it emerges exclusively under electron-doped conditions, while remaining suppressed for hole-doped SrIrO3. Our results establish that this response originates from an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven mechanism governed by polarity-controlled band filling of SrIrO3. These findings shift interfacial polarity from a passive structural consequence to an active design variable for engineering topological quantum states in oxide heterostructures.

papers.title: Supermoiré Formation and Robust Topological Edge State in Helical Trilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: When two materials with nearly matched lattice constants meet, they form commensurate domains separated by incommensurate domain walls that absorb the mismatch. Recently, this picture has been extended to moiré lattices: when two moiré superlattices have nearly equal periodicities, they can form a "supermoiré" consisting of commensurate moiré domains separated by domain walls. Helical trilayer graphene (HTG) is a particularly interesting example: theory predicts that its commensurate domains are distinct topological insulators, separated by a network of conducting domain walls. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to visualize supermoiré domains and their electronic properties in HTG at a twist angle of $\sim1.7^\circ$. We find atomic-scale evidence of relaxation into supermoiré domains, each hosting flat bands separated from remote bands by large gaps of $\sim40$ meV. Domain walls exhibit spectrally uniform edge states along their length, in excellent agreement with calculations for valley-protected topological edge modes. The topological character of the flat bands is intimately tied to wavefunction localization on a graphene sublattice, and we reveal the topological change across a domain boundary by imaging the reversal of sublattice polarization.

papers.title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
papers.abstract: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system. This basic idea is an inequality involving the purity of the original Gibbs state and a dual Gibbs state that is defined via space-time rotation. Here we consider a few generalizations of this purity bootstrap argument. We first extend it to arbitrary spatial dimensions. Our main result uses the space-time duality between symmetry generators and symmetry twists to obtain upper bounds on the splitting of nearly degenerate low-energy states, together with a nonzero gap above them, from finite-system information. As applications, we show that finite-system calculations for the 2+1-D toric code in a field and the 2+1-D transverse-field Ising model establish parameter regimes with four and two low-lying states whose splittings are bounded from above by $e^{-cL}$ and $e^{-cL^2}$ respectively for arbitrarily large system size $L$, while the gap above these states remains nonzero in the thermodynamic limit. Next, we extend it to fermionic systems and use a finite calculation to establish a symmetric mass generation phase in a $2+1$-D fermionic model. Finally, we apply the bootstrap to tensor-network states and establish exponential decay of connected correlations of all local operators in the symmetric square-lattice spin-one state introduced by Jian and Zaletel.

papers.title: $1/N$ corrections to $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in the critical $O(N)$ vector and Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models
papers.abstract: We compute the subleading corrections in the $1/N$ expansion of the three-point functions $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in the three-dimensional critical $O(N)$ vector and Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models. We determine the coefficients of the two parity-even conformal structures and the corresponding conformal collider parameters. The calculation uses an expansion of momentum-space Feynman diagrams in a soft external momentum, together with the contact terms required by background gauge and metric sources. The sums of the structure coefficients reproduce the known current and stress-tensor two-point normalizations. We also compute these coefficients independently using the metric and mixed metric--gauge derivatives of the sphere free energy. Extrapolating the large $N$ results to the $O(2)$ vector model yields reasonably good agreement with recent numerical bootstrap bounds. At $N=2$, our $γ$ and $t_4$ predictions lie within the joint bootstrap region under weaker spectral assumptions; their deviations from the more restrictive interval midpoints are only $3.28\%$ and $4.44\%$, respectively. We discuss the implications for energy flux, high-frequency conductivity, and shear response near quantum criticality.

papers.title: Observable-Based Learning of Effective Entanglement Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Determining the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) of an interacting quantum many-body system remains a fundamental challenge beyond special analytically tractable cases. Here we develop an observable-matching framework for learning effective EHs, which we demonstrate using response estimates from quantum Monte Carlo. As applications of this framework, we first calibrate the overall prefactor of the lattice Bisognano--Wichmann (LBW) construction using equal-time correlations and then learn spatially resolved couplings beyond its prescribed profile, without assuming a specific functional form for their spatial dependence. Trained solely on local correlations, the learned EHs reproduce benchmarked von Neumann and second Rényi entropies in $1$D and second Rényi entropies in $2$D. For a strong-bond cut associated with special surface criticality at the $(2+1)$D $O(3)$ Wilson--Fisher critical point, free-form learning outperforms the calibrated LBW ansatz in predicting the second Rényi entropy and reveals spatially nonuniform coupling renormalizations. Importantly, the learned EH also provides access to the von Neumann entropy in this setting, revealing a negative subleading correction and extending previous Rényi entropy findings to the von Neumann case. Directly evaluating the von Neumann entropy in such $(2+1)$D interacting quantum many-body systems remains challenging for conventional numerical methods. These results establish observable-based learning as a route to constructing effective entanglement Hamiltonians beyond prescribed spatial profiles in higher-dimensional interacting systems.

papers.title: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable
papers.abstract: The frustration-free property is valuable in quantum many-body systems, which states that its ground states simultaneously minimize all local interaction terms, even when these terms act on overlapping degrees of freedom. Prominent examples include the AKLT model and Kitaev's toric code model, which serve as paradigmatic models of symmetry-protected topological phases and topological order, respectively. A fundamental question is whether a given Hamiltonian is frustration-free for all system sizes. Here we establish two seemingly contradictory results concerning this decision problem. First, we prove that frustration-freeness is decidable for any fixed local Hilbert space dimension. Specifically, there exists a finite, Hamiltonian-independent system-size cutoff such that frustration-freeness at this cutoff size guarantees frustration-freeness at all system sizes. Second, on the other hand, we also show that there exists a frustration-free Hamiltonian whose frustration-freeness cannot be proved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC). We reconcile these seemingly contradictory results by showing that the cutoff, although finite for each local Hilbert space dimension, is uncomputable as a function of that dimension. Our findings reveal an unexpected fundamental distinction between decidability and provability arising in quantum many-body physics.

papers.title: Background Effects on Thermal Free Energy in Conformal Field Theories
papers.abstract: We compute background corrections to the thermal free energy of free conformal field theories (CFTs) with a global abelian symmetry defined on a box with all sides infinitely long by turning on a flat gauge field in general dimensions. This result is applied to the U(N) maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, the ABJ(M) theory, and the free U(N) vector model in four, three, and two spacetime dimensions, respectively. In these examples, the thermal free energies monotonically increase as the background field does, and cross a zero within the valid range. We argue that the systems undergo a phase transition at the zero, where the effective degrees of freedom fall off similarly to the color-confinement one, and that it always occurs if the number of matter fields is greater than a critical value. We comment for this phase transition to circumvent the Mermin-Wagner-Coleman theorem in two spacetime dimensions.

papers.title: Electrically tunable superconducting dimensionality in stripe-ordered monolayer MoTe$_2$
papers.abstract: Dimensionality governs the stability of collective quantum states, including whether Cooper pairs can establish the phase coherence required for superconductivity. In solids, however, electronic dimensionality is usually encoded in the crystal structure and is difficult to control reversibly. Here we show evidence that monolayer 1$T^{\prime}$-MoTe$_2$ develops a stripe charge-density wave that reorganizes its low-energy electronic states into quasi-one-dimensional channels. Raman spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy identify the stripe order, whereas directional transport and tunneling spectroscopy reveal superconducting correlations confined to the stripe direction and insulating behavior perpendicular to it. Electrostatic doping weakens the transverse insulating response and drives the system into phase-coherent two-dimensional superconductivity. These results show that stripe charge order can reconfigure superconducting dimensionality and make it electrically tunable within a single crystalline layer.

papers.title: Interacting particles crossing barriers: spatial statistics, choice of route taken and role of interactions
papers.abstract: We consider the statistics of pairs of particles moving in a potential energy landscape exhibiting a choice of different pathways from a local minimum start point to the global energy minimum destination. We examine the impact of both attractive and repulsive interactions between the particles, treating these via either a soft Gaussian or a Lennard-Jones potential. We investigate the statistics of which particle arrives at the destination first, arrival-time distributions and where in the system the second particle is located when the first arrives. We find that the typical arrival time of the first particle can be significantly different to that of a single particle, sometimes being much longer and in other cases being shorter, depending on the nature of the particle interactions. In the case of soft Gaussian attractive interactions, which effectively bind the pair of particles together to form a single larger particle, the arrival time can be much longer, since bigger particles cross barriers more slowly. In contrast, the arrival time is shorter when there is a repulsive core interaction between the particles, due to excluded-area and particle-ordering effects. We investigate the probability distribution of particles' positions through the Jensen--Shannon divergence which unveils the dependence of the spatial distribution of the particles within the confining potential on the parameters of the particle interaction potentials.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.

papers.title: Typical number and stability of equilibria in large non-reciprocal complex systems
papers.abstract: We consider a prototypical class of dynamics of $N\gg 1$ degrees of freedom subject to two competing terms, one favoring relaxation to a trivial equilibrium and one taking the form of a Gaussian force field promoting the emergence of many local equilibria. The latter is a non-gradient field, i.e. it includes a non-reciprocal component with a tunable strength. For this model, we compute the quenched complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the typical number of equilibria, resolved by stability index. We compare it with the annealed complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the average number of equilibria. We show that the two coincide only in the fully non-reciprocal limit: for any finite degree of reciprocity, typical realizations contain exponentially fewer equilibria than predicted by the average count. Increasing reciprocity enhances the discrepancy between the two. The quenched complexity depends explicitly on the covariance of the random force field and on the degree of non-reciprocity: the universality observed at the annealed level breaks down. The average counting of equilibria correctly identifies the location of the topology trivialization transition, but it does not capture the typical organization of equilibria near this transition, nor the stability index of the dominant equilibria.

papers.title: Active model B+ from run-and-tumble particles on a triangular lattice
papers.abstract: Active model B+ (AMB+) explains how motility-induced phase separation can be arrested by reverse Ostwald ripening, but its coefficients have not been derived from a microscopic lattice model that shows it. We provide an exact hydrodynamic description of a six-polarity lattice gas on a hexagonal geometry and employ a full gradient expansion with angular-harmonic elimination to rigorously derive AMB+ with every coefficient fixed by the Péclet number Pe. Near the critical point (3/4, 4), coarsening is ordinary; further away, field theory predicts reverse Ostwald ripening of vapor bubbles above Pe $> 4 \sqrt{3}$, and simulations show long-lived bubbly states.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Speed and Efficiency with Quantum Feedback
papers.abstract: Rapid thermodynamic operations generally entail irreversible dissipation, giving rise to trade-offs between operating speed and thermodynamic cost. Yet, how quantum feedback fundamentally reshapes these trade-offs remains elusive. Here, we derive a finite-time current--dissipation relation for continuously monitored open quantum dynamics with jump feedback. From this fundamental relation, we establish a quantum speed limit and a power-efficiency trade-off for stationary information engines, identifying how feedback affects state transformations and the performance of engines through both informational entropy and direct dynamical contributions. Our results provide a quantitative foundation for fast, low-dissipation quantum thermodynamics in the presence of feedback control, exemplified by attaining the generalized Landauer bound in finite-time information erasure and approaching unit information efficiency at finite power in the large-system limit of a collective engine.

papers.title: Thermodynamic geometry of three coupled Ising spins: exact curvature, frustration and bond anisotropy
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic curvature is widely used as a diagnostic of interactions and phase transitions, yet its interpretation is usually tested only in the thermodynamic limit. Small spin clusters are physically relevant in their own right, since a macroscopic sample of independent molecular trimers or a few-qubit quantum simulator is governed exactly by the few-spin partition function. They also provide the only setting in which the geometry can be obtained in closed form together with its full dependence on the interaction topology. We study the Fisher-Rao (Ruppeiner) geometry of three Ising spins with arbitrary pairwise couplings in a longitudinal field. This cluster interpolates continuously between an open chain and a geometrically frustrated triangle. For the symmetric triangle we obtain the scalar curvature in closed form. It vanishes on the noninteracting line and on a line of fixed field-to-temperature ratio that does not depend on the coupling, which coincides with the inflection point of the single-spin susceptibility. The near-zero behaviour is therefore exactly linear and reflects analyticity rather than critical scaling. In the frustrated antiferromagnetic regime the curvature remains finite and negative down to zero temperature. A general low-temperature formula relates this plateau to the change in magnetization content between the degenerate ground manifold and its first excitation. Any bond anisotropy destroys the plateau below a crossover temperature that depends only logarithmically on the anisotropy, so the curvature is an extremely sensitive detector of exact ground-state degeneracy. On the ferromagnetic side the zero-temperature curvature is universal for all couplings, whereas additional zero lines in anisotropic clusters track field-induced crossings of excited levels.

papers.title: First-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges
papers.abstract: We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behaviour with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric wedge formed by a vertical and an inclined wall. The DFT calculations confirm the two condensed morphologies predicted for the symmetric wedge and the three morphologies predicted for the asymmetric wedge and their emergence depending on the wedge size, opening angle, and wall contact angle. Under partial-wetting conditions, the microscopic phase boundaries are in nearly perfect quantitative agreement with the macroscopic predictions, including reentrant changes between pinned and depinned meniscus configurations and the appearance of the semi-double-pinned state in the asymmetric wedge. Under complete-wetting conditions, the DFT phase diagrams retain the topology predicted by the macroscopic theory, but the single-pinned region is systematically enlarged. This shift is attributed to adsorbed liquid films, which reduce the effective width available to the gas and thereby increase the effective aspect ratio of the confinement.

papers.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently. We show that this trade-off maps onto the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. (i) For any data, the error of parallel generation is the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. (ii) For Markov data, generation is a random sequential adsorption process with labelled gaps, which we solve exactly for any number of steps. (iii) For many steps, the error becomes the dissipation of a slowly driven system: the unmasking schedule plays the role of the driving protocol, the number of steps that of its duration, and the error is set by a thermodynamic metric that we obtain in closed form from the mutual information between tokens. Optimal schedules are geodesics of this metric. The exact solution shows how correlations in the text shape both the error and the quality of the output. The longer the correlations, the more the error concentrates at the start of generation. Schedules that start with small steps then gain more, both in path error and in perplexity, and need fewer steps to reach their asymptotic behaviour.

papers.title: Emergent Symmetry in Constant-Density Flocks
papers.abstract: In two dimensions, the ordered phase of constant-density flocks is described by a single angle field, which makes them arguably the simplest systems with a scale-free ordered phase of collective motion. We show that the equation governing the corresponding Nambu-Goldstone mode, completed with terms previously discarded, possesses on large scales an invariance combining a shear and a Galilean boost. Broken at the bare level, this symmetry is restored at the unique attractive fixed point, and the associated Ward identities fix the scaling exponents exactly, as confirmed numerically.

papers.title: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
papers.abstract: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.

papers.title: Exact and Near-Exact Inverse Renormalization Group with Constrained Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: We establish conditions for exactness of the inverse renormalization group via constrained Markov processes, a class of Monte Carlo simulations which sample the degrees of freedom within a block on a fine lattice under the constraint that they remain consistent with the corresponding degree of freedom on the coarse lattice according to a forward renormalization group transformation. We show analytically, for an arbitrary transformation, that constrained Markov processes correspond to an exact inversion of the renormalization group at the fixed point action, and to a near-exact inversion in the vicinity of the fixed point. We then optimize renormalization group transformations directly on inversely renormalized configurations to effectively map the action onto itself and ensure computational stability in the generation of configurations for high-dimensional systems. Starting from a set of uncorrelated configurations for the three-dimensional $φ^{4}$ quantum field theory at lattice volume $V=16^{3}$, we invert the renormalization group with constrained Monte Carlo to construct a set of uncorrelated, near-equilibrium configurations for $V=128^{3}$ and extract two critical exponents of the system. The inversion exhibits no critical slowing down, with dynamic critical exponent $z=0.03(2)$.

papers.title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
papers.abstract: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium orientational bistability of a magnetically-driven slender particle
papers.abstract: Externally driven systems are non-equilibrium but accessible to stationary states. By combining theoretical calculations and particle-based simulations, we investigate the orientational configuration of a transversely-magnetized slender particle in a rotating magnetic field. Our results reveal nonequilibrium orientational bistability in both regimes that the particle rotates synchronously and asynchronously with the field. The relative populations of standing and lying orientations depend strongly on the driving frequency in the synchronous regime, whereas they are primarily controlled by the magnetic field strength in the asynchronous regime. Effective free-energy approximations further capture the principal features of the steady-state orientational distributions in both regimes. Our work aims to give a statistical-thermodynamic description of orientational bistability in magnetically-driven slender particles, paving the way for relevant experimental designs and advanced applications.

papers.title: Autotaxis of a Run-and-Tumble Agent via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We study the run-tumble motion of a single autochemotactic agent that secretes and senses chemical cues using a reinforcement learning (RL) framework. In a chemical environment that changes dynamically via secretion, diffusion, and degradation of attractant chemicals, we study the effectiveness of RL for a successful navigation strategy. We show that RL enhances chemotactic performance. Starting from a random initial position, the probability of finding the agent in the favorable region (near the attractant peak) increases faster with time and reaches a higher value in the long time limit when RL is used, compared to the case when the agent performs usual run-tumble chemotaxis without using RL. We also characterize the chemotactic performance of the agent by varying different parameters like rates of secretion, degradation, and diffusion. Importantly, we observe a non-monotonic dependence of the chemotactic performance on the learning and exploration rates, indicating the existence of an optimal RL strategy for the most efficient navigation. We explain these observations as a result of the interplay between the pre-existing attractant environment and the agent-generated attractant profile.

papers.title: Electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium: discretization and effective medium approximation
papers.abstract: The effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium is studied within a discretization scheme and the effective-medium approximation (EMA). A square lattice is superimposed on a random isotropic medium; each cell is assigned the conductivity of its majority component, and the cell is replaced by a star of four resistors. Neighboring cells are connected by an equivalent resistor whose conductivity is $σ_1$, $σ_2$, or the harmonic mean $σ_{12}=2σ_1σ_2/(σ_1+σ_2)$, with probabilities $(1-p)^2$, $p^2$, and $2p(1-p)$, respectively. Applying Foster's theorem and the EMA yields a closed equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity $x$ and, after transformation, a cubic equation whose coefficients depend on $p$ and the conductivity ratio $r$. The EMA predictions are compared with direct calculations on a $200\times200$ resistor network with periodic lateral boundary conditions and Dirichlet conditions on the top and bottom. For uncorrelated disorder, good agreement is found. For correlated disorder, when resistor conductivities are assigned according to the discretization rule from the colors of adjacent nodes, significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of $1/2$. The results question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain discrepancies previously reported for random nanowire networks.

papers.title: Percolation of discorectangles oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions
papers.abstract: The percolation of finite-thickness elongated objects---discorectangles (stadiums)---oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions is studied, extending recent results for zero-thickness sticks. The angular distribution is the ``Maltese cross'' parametrized by $α$. Based on the known analytic expression for the excluded area of a discorectangle pair, the percolation threshold is estimated by the eigenvalue method. The discorectangle connectivity matrix is represented as the stick matrix plus a rank-1 term determined by the constant part of the excluded area, $C=4lw+πw^{2}$, which gives the approximate relations $λ_{\max}^{\mathrm{DR}}\approxλ_{\max}^{\mathrm{stick}}+C$ and $n_c^{\mathrm{DR}}\approx n_c^{\mathrm{stick}}/(1+C n_c^{\mathrm{stick}})$. Finite thickness shifts the absolute thresholds and affects the first normalization, whereas the second normalization, written through maximum eigenvalues, cancels the additive geometric contribution and preserves only the orientational dependence, explaining the universality of the normalized curves. Monte Carlo simulations of unit-length discorectangles with aspect ratios 8, 16, and 32, various domain sizes, periodic boundary conditions, and union--find scaling analysis confirm the theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Unraveling square and kagome lattice frustrated magnetism by scalable tensor networks
papers.abstract: We extend the scalability of variational infinite two-dimensional tensor network methods with application to investigate frustrated magnetism of the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model and kagome-lattice Heisenberg model. In the sign-problem-free limit of the square-lattice model, we achieve high ground-state energy precision comparable to quantum Monte Carlo methods. With no obstruction beyond this limit, our method obtains direct estimates of order parameters. For the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model, we determine isotropic plaquette order in the valence-bond solid region. For the model near $J_2/J_1=0.5$, and the kagome lattice Heisenberg model, our data indicate linear-dispersion gapless states. To probe the candidate spin-liquid nature of the highly frustrated cases, we go beyond inferring the absence of symmetry-breaking orders and analyze susceptibilities that characterize gapless spin liquids. By estimating scaling dimensions, our data indicate a stable gapless spin liquid on the kagome lattice, and competing scenarios for the intermediate regime of the square-lattice model. Our developments include parallelization and randomized low-rank methods and largely expand the frontier of high-precision variational numerics for quantum phases of matter.

papers.title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
papers.abstract: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.

papers.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
papers.abstract: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
papers.abstract: We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit. The equal-time commutators of the boundary current with the spatial components of the gauge-invariant field strength vanish, so microcausality is satisfied; when the boundary parameters are such that the two boundary sectors decouple, its retarded response vanishes at all times. Locally, the boundary constraints are solved by $w_i=\partial_iχ$ and $h_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_jξ+η_{ij}φ$. When the boundary parameters are such that the two sectors decouple, the induced action is the direct sum of a chiral boson in the $w_i$ sector and a higher-rank sector in which $φ$ is auxiliary and $ψ=\partial_1ξ$ is the propagating field. The latter has a non-chiral Luttinger description on its positive-energy branch and admits a chiral reduction. The boundary conditions determine the velocity and positivity branch of the $w_i$ mode, while the compatibility analysis in the $h_{ij}$ sector selects the positive-energy branch. On the positive-energy branch the two chiral modes co-propagate with orientation opposite to the sign of $κ$.

papers.title: Local Correlations Determine the Dephasing Threshold of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology
papers.abstract: In this work, we try to understand the question of how to address the survival of band topology in the presence of dephasing. We investigate this question in the Kane-Mele $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological insulator. To determine the stability of the topological invariant we construct a single particle Hamiltonian that also provides identical correlation at the single particle level. The phase transition from topological to trivial is determined by the gap closing of this correlation Hamiltonian. This gap closing is related to purity gap. As a diagnostics we calculated the invariant directly and as a complementary diagnostic, coherent two-terminal transport through the auxiliary correlation Hamiltonian exhibits quantized conductance in the nontrivial region. This does not establish physical conductance under dephasing. Our results identify a predictive local criterion for the survival of single-particle topological structure under a specified noise channel.

papers.title: Coexistence of antiferromagnetism and topological $s+d+id$ superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between antiferromagnetism and topological superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers. We demonstrate how topological $s+d+id$ superconductivity is induced by a twist of $θ\sim 45^\circ$ in a microscopic $t$-$J$ type model of cuprate bilayers, where it robustly coexists with antiferromagnetic order at low hole doping. This novel pairing state becomes physically accessible at realistic interlayer couplings in the overdoped regime. Crucially, it displays a characteristic $2$-fold rotational symmetry in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) not observed in the competing time-reversal symmetry breaking $d+id$ or $s+id$ states previously found. A finite Josephson effect at $45^\circ$ twist together with signatures in scanning tunneling spectroscopy of its two Majorana edge modes identifies this topological $s+d+id$ state unambiguously.

papers.title: Optimal performance of driven-dissipative many-body quantum batteries beyond complete nonreciprocity
papers.abstract: Proposals for nonreciprocal quantum batteries identify the point of complete nonreciprocity, where coherent and reservoir-mediated couplings balance, as the operating point for enhanced charging. We show that, for batteries built from interacting qubits, this point is, in general, suboptimal. The optimal design is set by a more intricate interplay between the coherent coupling and the local and collective dissipation rates, of which complete nonreciprocity is only a special case. We consider a many-body battery charged by a driven many-body charger, with each qubit coupled to a local bath and the complete setup immersed in a shared engineered reservoir. For a weakly driven two-qubit setup, we prove the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction to be the optimal coupling, and show that the battery capacity is maximized at a coupling strength fixed by the local and collective dissipation rates, which coincides with complete nonreciprocity only for a specific balance between them. The shared reservoir enhances the capacity for couplings weaker or stronger than both local dissipation rates, and can increase the extractable work even where it reduces the capacity. At strong drive, with the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction between the charger and the battery, the capacity is bounded by $1/2$. For qubits arranged in a star network with a single central battery qubit, these results remain qualitatively unchanged, while the maximum capacity of a battery charged by $N_A$ weakly driven charger qubits saturates with $N_A$ in the presence of the shared reservoir, approaching its limit as $N_A^{-1}$. In contrast, the maximum capacity of $N_B$ qubit batteries charged by a single-qubit charger decays as $N_B^{-2}$.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Phase Diagrams in $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaBr$_x$Cl$_{4-x}$ under Physical and Chemical Pressure
papers.abstract: The evolution of electron correlation in the superconducting state of the mixed-crystal series $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaBr$_x$Cl$_{4-x}$ was investigated by magnetic and transport measurements. Br concentrations evaluated by electron-probe microanalysis agree well with single-crystal X-ray diffraction refinement. Demagnetization-corrected susceptibility and magnetization of crystals with $x_{c(rf)}$ = 0.22, 0.24, 0.42, and 0.63 all show a diamagnetic superconducting transition. The lower critical field $H_{c1}$, determined from the deviation from the Meissner response, shows a dome-like maximum at $x_{c(rf)}$ = 0.24. The upper critical field $H_{c2}$, obtained from the first high-field magnetoresistance measurements in this system, decreases with increasing Br concentration up to $x_{c(rf)}$ = 0.42, establishing the high-field superconducting boundary on the chemical-pressure side. Combining these results with reported transport data under chemical and physical pressure, we propose a pressure-temperature phase diagram for $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$. Its double-dome-like structure has a local minimum near x = 0, where a quantum-critical point was proposed at P $\approx$ 0.13 GPa, separating a low-pressure regime of superconductivity coexisting with magnetism and an unconventional metallic state from a higher-pressure regime with conventional metallic behavior. A low-temperature resistivity upturn, previously reported only under physical pressure, is also found under chemical pressure, suggesting that spin-density-wave fluctuations may extend continuously across both pressure axes. The phase diagram overlaps with that of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ under physical pressure, indicating that chemical substitution, external pressure, and molecular substitution can be unified in a single bandwidth-controlled phase diagram for $λ$-type molecular superconductors.

papers.title: Exploring Variational Regularization of Krylov Subspaces
papers.abstract: Krylov subspace methods efficiently approximate extremal eigenstates and eigenvalues of many-body Hamiltonians, but non-orthogonal bases can suffer from ill-conditioning. This challenge is amplified in quantum computing, where direct state access and thus straightforward orthogonalization are unavailable. We investigate a variational Krylov-like framework that iteratively optimizes a parametrized sequence of states to mimic Lanczos-like couplings while penalizing linear dependencies. Analyzed against exact Krylov and Lanczos on a finite Anderson impurity model, ansatz expressivity strongly influences the performance: Hamiltonian-inspired ansätze preserve Krylov-like convergence while improving the conditioning, whereas shallow ansätze remain stable but miss low-energy directions.

papers.title: Pressure-induced symmetry breaking and polarity in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr
papers.abstract: The van der Waals magnet CrSBr has emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring coupled structural, magnetic, and electronic phenomena. Yet, the evolution of its crystal symmetry and electronic states under pressure and temperature remains unresolved. To elucidate this we employ low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman scattering and photoluminescence measurements under hydrostatic pressures of up to 12 GPa, complemented by first-principles calculations.We observe a cascade of pressure-induced structural transitions from the orthorhombic $Pmmn$ to monoclinic $P2_1/m$ phase at $\approx$ 1.5 GPa, followed by the emergence of a polar orthorhombic $Pmm$2 phase $\approx$ 6.5 GPa. The change in symmetry is accompanied by phonon anomalies and a direct-to-indirect bandgap crossover. Our results demonstrate pressure as a knob to engineer structure, symmetry and electronic properties in CrSBr in a coupled manner.

papers.title: Lefschetz-Thimble Method to the Sign Problem in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
papers.abstract: The sign problem in path integrals severely limits the application of quantum Monte Carlo methods to strongly correlated systems, whereas the Lefschetz-thimble method offers a rigorous framework to mitigate this issue. In this paper, we establish a numerical framework based on the Lefschetz thimbles for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. By introducing continuous auxiliary fields via the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, the partition function is formulated as a high-dimensional complex integral. We employ the complex Langevin equation to explore the saddle-point distribution of the effective action in the complex plane. Monte Carlo integration is then performed to compute the partition function and Green functions. Our numerical results exhibit excellent agreement with high-temperature expansions, infrared-limit solutions, and determinantal quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations, confirming the validity of our framework. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our complex Langevin search successfully captures the relevant dominant saddle points governing the SYK model in the large-N limit. Our work deepens the understanding of the sign problem in the SYK model and provides a viable non-perturbative avenue for addressing sign problems in more complex strongly correlated systems.

papers.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Rényi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
papers.abstract: Free fermions exhibit Eigenstate Typicality (ET) meaning that the reduced density matrix, $ρ$, of a small spatial subsystem of a {\sl single}, typical, excited energy eigenstate is gaussian with a modular hamiltonian, $h \equiv -\log ρ$, asymptotically proportional to the free fermion hamiltonian. In effect, the ET may be thought of as providing an independent route to establishing the Fermi-Dirac (FD) distribution for free fermions. We revisit this argument for fermions belonging to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates. Specifically, we show that the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates in a 1-d free fermion lattice system is interacting, and therefore the reduced density matrix for the subsystem is not gaussian. Measurements of the single particle distribution of a small subsystem would then exhibit non-thermal deviations from the FD distribution. These features may be traced to a violation of Wick's theorem for the chosen excited state. We develop a perturbation theory for the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a weak mixture of degenerate states and study the modular hamiltonian (exactly) computationally. Finally, we speculate that initial conditions in a realistic fermi system evolving towards equilibrium might be encoded in the interaction terms of the modular hamiltonian and consequent correlations of fermions.

papers.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
papers.abstract: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems.
